t.Como otimizar o Google Meu Negócio: o gu: How to optimize your Google Business Profile: the complete guide (2026)
t.O seu perfil do Google (hoje gerenciado: Your Google profile (now managed through Google Business Profile, formerly Google My Business) is your business's most-viewed storefront — more than your website, more than Instagram. It's what shows up when someone searches "near me", and every field you fill in is a signal Google uses to decide whether to show you or your competitor. This is the longest guide on our blog: it walks through the profile section by section, explains what each one does for your ranking and shows what to prioritize first.
t.Um aviso honesto antes de começar: não e: An honest warning before we start: there's no magic button and no guaranteed first place. What there is, is the right signals adding up over time. Those who fill in everything, keep it up to date and steadily gather real reviews tend to rise; those who set up a half-done profile and disappear fall behind. Treat this guide as a maintenance checklist, not a one-time trick.
t.1. Nome do negócio: exatamente como na f: 1. Business name: exactly as it appears on your storefront
t.Parece o campo mais simples, e é justame: It looks like the simplest field, and that's exactly where many people slip up. Google's rule is clear: the name must be the business's real name, the same as on the storefront and the paperwork. No stuffing keywords and the city in there — "Padaria do Zé" can't become "Padaria do Zé Best Fresh Bread Downtown São Paulo".
t.Além de ser contra as regras (e passível: Besides being against the rules (and grounds for suspension), keyword stuffing in the name makes the profile look like spam and can trigger reports from competitors. If your real name already contains the category — "Oficina Mecânica São Jorge" (São Jorge Auto Repair) — great, that's legitimate. What doesn't fly is making it up.
t.2. Categoria: o campo que mais decide se: 2. Category: the field that most decides whether you show up
t.A descrição (até 750 caracteres) aparece: The description (up to 750 characters) appears in the "About" tab. It weighs less in ranking than the category, but it helps customers understand who you are and gives Google context. Write in natural language, start with what you do and for whom, mention your main services and the area you serve. Use the words your customers would actually use when looking for you.
t.Evite encher de palavra-chave repetida,: Avoid stuffing it with repeated keywords, promotions (which change) and links — Google strips links from the description. Think of it as the "about" you'd tell a customer who has never heard of you: honest, specific and jargon-free.
t.4. Fotos: o que mais move a decisão de q: 4. Photos: what most drives the decision of people who already found you
t.Fotos não são enfeite — são um dos fator: Photos aren't decoration — they're one of the factors that most influence whether someone who found your profile actually clicks, calls or comes to you. Profiles with good, recent photos get more interactions, and interaction is a signal of prominence.
t.5. Produtos e serviços: seu catálogo den: 5. Products and services: your catalog inside Google
t.Uma clínica lista as consultas e exames;: A clinic lists its appointments and tests; a store lists its product lines; a service provider lists each service with a price range. Put care into the descriptions using real search terms. Keep it up to date: old prices and services you no longer offer cause frustration and bad reviews.
t.6. Atributos: os detalhes que aparecem e: 6. Attributes: the details that show up in filtered searches
t.Atributos são as marcações do tipo \"ace: Attributes are tags like "accepts cards", "wheelchair accessible", "free Wi-Fi", "parking", "pet friendly", "offers delivery". They seem small, but they feed the filters customers use — someone searching "restaurant with parking" only sees those who ticked that attribute. There are also identity attributes (women-led business, for example) that get highlighted for people who value them.
t.Marque com sinceridade tudo que se aplic: Honestly tick everything that applies. Each attribute is a new doorway through which the right customer can arrive. Ticking something you don't offer only brings an unhappy customer to your door.
t.Se você tem horários diferentes por serv: If you have different hours per service (pickup, delivery, counter), use the more detailed hours fields when available. Accuracy here is respect for people who made the trip.
t.8. Posts do Google: sinal de perfil ativ: 8. Google posts: a sign of an active profile
t.Posts têm prazo de validade curto na exi: Posts have a short display life, so the value is in consistency, not in one perfect standalone post. Include an image and an action button ("learn more", "call", "book") when it makes sense.
t.9. Perguntas e respostas: assuma o contr: 9. Questions and answers: take control before the customer does
t.Monitore a seção e responda o quanto ant: Monitor the section and answer any new question as soon as possible. A quick, polite answer keeps wrong information from sitting there steering readers' decisions.
t.11. Avaliações: o fator que puxa tudo pr: 11. Reviews: the factor that pulls everything up
t.Deixamos por último de propósito, porque: We left it for last on purpose, because it's the most decisive — and the one most people neglect after tidying up their listing. Reviews influence ranking (prominence), influence whether people who already found you click, and even influence which attributes and services Google highlights. Volume, rating, recency and your response rate all count.
t.Três pilares aqui, e nenhum deles admite: Three pillars here, and none of them allows shortcuts:
t.A ordem de prioridade: por onde começar: The order of priority: where to start
t.Se você não vai fazer tudo hoje, faça ne: If you're not going to do it all today, do it in this order. First, what blocks you from showing up: profile verification, the correct primary category and accurate hours. Then, what drives clicks from people who already found you: good, recent photos and a flow of reviews. Only then the extras that refine relevance: secondary categories, products and services, attributes, description, posts and questions.
t.Traduzindo em rotina: uma faxina inicial: Turned into a routine: an initial listing clean-up (one well-spent afternoon) and then light maintenance every week — a new photo, a post, replying to the reviews and questions that came in, checking that the week's hours are right. Consistency is what separates the profile that rises from the one that stalls.
t.Como saber se a otimização está funciona: How to know if the optimization is working
t.Preencher tudo é metade do trabalho; a o: Filling everything in is half the job; the other half is measuring. The profile's own dashboard shows how many people saw you, which searches they came from and how many called, asked for directions or clicked through to your website. Track these numbers and watch whether the trend rises as you keep the profile active.

A complete listing gets you out of a disadvantage; steady maintenance and real, honest reviews are what, over time, push your business up in the searches that bring actual customers. Start with what blocks you from showing up, win the click with photos and reviews, and keep the pace.

h.Antes de mergulhar campo a campo, vale e: Before diving in field by field, it's worth understanding why optimizing the profile works. Google decides what to show in a local search by crossing three factors: relevance (how well your business matches what the person searched for), distance (where you are relative to the searcher) and prominence (how well-known and active your business appears). You can't change distance, but almost everything in this guide pushes the other two. A complete, active profile gives Google more reasons and more context to put you up front.
h.Faça isto primeiro: confirme que o seu p: Do this first: make sure your profile is verified and that you have admin access. Without verification, many of the fields below stay locked and Google gives the profile less weight. Search your business name on Google while signed in to the right account and look for the "Your business profile" panel.
h.Se há um único campo pra acertar, é este: If there's one field to get right, it's this one. The primary category is what tells Google most about which searches you should appear in. A coffee shop listed as "Restaurant" misses the searches of people looking for "coffee shop near me" — and those are different searches, with different competitors.
h.Escolha a categoria principal mais espec: Choose the most specific, accurate primary category that describes your business, not the broadest one. Then add secondary categories for everything else you do: a bakery that serves lunch can be "Bakery" (primary) + "Restaurant" and "Coffee shop" (secondary). Don't overdo it by adding categories that don't represent the business — that confuses Google and attracts the wrong customer.
h.Como descobrir a categoria certa: busque: How to find the right category: look up three or four competitors that already rank well in your city and see how they're categorized. If everyone who ranks is "X" and you're "Y", it's worth reconsidering. Mirroring those already at the top is a good starting point.
h.O básico que todo perfil deveria ter: lo: The basics every profile should have: logo, cover photo, storefront (so people recognize it on the street), interior, team, and your products or services in detail. A repair shop shows its service area and the team in uniform; a salon shows before-and-after shots of real work; a restaurant shows well-photographed dishes and a full dining room (with permission from those who appear).
h.Fotos reais, tiradas no local, batem fot: Real photos, taken on site, beat stock photos every time — they build trust and Google values freshness. Add new photos regularly: a profile that gets new images every month looks alive. It's also worth keeping an eye on the photos customers post and making sure your better ones are featured.
h.A seção de produtos e a de serviços deix: The products and services sections let you list what you offer item by item, with name, description and price. This helps in two ways: it gives Google more context about what you do (boosting relevance) and answers the customer's question before they even get in touch — "do you do this? how much is it?".
h.Horário errado é uma das maiores fontes: Wrong hours are one of the biggest sources of negative reviews: the customer trusts Google, makes the trip and finds the door closed. Keep your regular hours always correct and, more importantly, add special hours for holidays and unusual dates. Google even flags "hours may differ on holidays" when you don't fill them in — and that lowers trust.
h.Os posts (novidades, ofertas, eventos) a: Posts (updates, offers, events) appear on your profile and show Google the business is active — which helps prominence. It doesn't need to become a social network: one update every week or two keeps the profile alive. Announce a real promotion, a new product, an event, a change in hours.
h.A seção de perguntas e respostas é públi: The questions and answers section is public and — an important detail — anyone can answer, including competitors or misinformed customers. That's why the best strategy is to seed the most common questions yourself ("do you have parking?", "do you take walk-ins?", "do you accept Pix?") and answer them with the correct information.
h.Ative o chat/mensagens se você consegue: Turn on chat/messages if you can reply quickly — slow replies frustrate people and Google measures your response time. Connect booking or reservations if your type of business allows it. And fill in the correct website and phone number: they're the profile's direct conversion paths, and Google uses the consistency of this data (name, address, phone) as a trust signal.
h.Volume constante. Um fluxo estável de av: Steady volume. A stable flow of new reviews is worth more than a one-off spike followed by months of nothing. Ten real reviews a month signal a living business; two hundred at once and then nothing signal the opposite — and Google is suspicious of artificial spikes.
h.Resposta a todas. Responder avaliações (: Reply to all of them. Replying to reviews (good and bad) shows Google and customers that you're present. Criticism answered with a cool head is worth more to readers than the rating itself.
h.Só avaliação legítima. Nada de comprar r: Legitimate reviews only. No buying reviews and no filtering who can review.
h.O que NÃO fazer, nunca: comprar avaliaçõ: What NEVER to do: buy reviews or practice review gating. Buying reviews is the fastest way to lose your rating all at once (Google detects them and removes them in bulk, sometimes suspending the profile). Review gating — filtering customers so only happy ones are sent to Google and unhappy ones are diverted — violates the platform's policies and puts the profile at risk. On top of that, hiding unhappy customers blinds you to real problems in your operation. The path that lasts is asking every satisfied customer for a review, always, with as little friction as possible.
h.O ponto cego mais comum é não saber onde: The most common blind spot is not knowing where you stand against competitors in your category and area. You might have a 4.6 and think it's great, while the top three in your neighborhood have a 4.8 with twice as many reviews — and that's why they show up ahead of you. Having this comparative picture turns "I think it's fine" into "I know exactly where I need to improve".
